sources.name: Axios

sources.description: Courts and governments worldwide felt the impact of this week's Microsoft outage, which sidelined work and stymied communication.

sources.name: Ars Technica
sources.title: Microsoft’s global outage may be worse than Amazon's or CrowdStrike's, expert says
sources.description: A global outage taking down a wide range of Microsoft 365 services remains ongoing Friday morning. The outage started midday Thursday, impacting users of Microsoft email, cloud, and AI services. Microsoft has documented the full list of services impacted by the error, while moving early Friday morning to protect customers around the world from losing emails during the extended disruptions.

sources.name: TIME
sources.title: Microsoft Struggles to Repair Worldwide Outage. Here's What You Need to Know
sources.description: The icons for a range of Microsoft apps, including Microsoft Outlook, seen on a laptop, in London, England, on Nov. 13, 2026. —Yui Mok—Getty Images An outage affecting Microsoft services including Outlook, Teams, and Copilot has stretched into a second day, leaving businesses and governments around the world struggling to access email communications.

sources.description: A Microsoft outage involving services like Outlook and Teams has dragged on for hours and impacted many users, companies and some government operations.

sources.name: NBC News
sources.title: Microsoft says major outage was due to 'a network capacity upgrade'
sources.description: Microsoft says a widespread outage they are still working on resolving was not caused by a cyberattack but by "a network capacity upgrade." NBC News' Christine Romans and TechRadar's Lance Ulanoff discuss how the outage is affecting businesses across the world.

sources.name: NBC News
sources.title: Microsoft Scrambles to Find Fix Massive Global Outage
sources.description: Workplaces, government agencies and schools around the globe were thrown into chaos after Microsoft’s servers went down Thursday afternoon. The massive outage is impacting the entire Microsoft suite of products including Outlook, Teams, Copilot and SharePoint. NBC’s Christine Romans reports for TODAY on the tech giant’s struggle to find a fix.

sources.name: Wired
sources.title: The Microsoft Outage Is a Warning for the World
sources.description: Countless businesses, schools, hospitals, and governments have found out the hard way what it means to rely on a single company’s systems to get things done. And next time could be even worse.

sources.name: The Verge
sources.title: Microsoft’s massive Outlook outage might be over
sources.description: Service is recovering for Microsoft Outlook and 365 after an almost two-day outage impacting millions of users around the world. While some apps and features are still running in a degraded state on Friday morning, some people (including Verge staffers) reported that access to their emails had been restored, though the flow of Outlook mail might be delayed.

sources.name: The New York Times
sources.title: Microsoft Says Outage Disrupting Outlook Is Improving
sources.description: Health services, schools, police departments and companies worldwide reported disruptions to their work. The cause was unclear, though Microsoft appeared to rule out a cyberattack.

sources.name: Semafor
sources.title: Microsoft reports progress in restoring service after global outage
sources.description: Microsoft reported progress, but not a full recovery, following an outage Thursday that affected Outlook, Teams, and Copilot across more than 70 countries. The consequences have been wide-reaching: Several police departments in the UK said Friday that the public shouldn’t report crimes via online submission forms, and should call them in instead.

sources.name: NPR
sources.title: Is Outlook down? Widespread outage hits Microsoft email and other apps
sources.description: A widespread outage has hit Microsoft platforms including Outlook, with many users encountering trouble using their email accounts.

sources.name: Wired
sources.title: Microsoft 365 Crawls Back to Life After a 24-Hour Outage
sources.description: The company says a bad update—not a cyberattack or AI—caused its servers around the world to crash.
